content:
If the supplier's plans come to fruition, some memory chips used in Apple products will be manufactured in the United States for the first time.

According to the latest report, Apple's memory supplier SK hynix is in discussions with Intel to use a chip fabrication plant that Intel plans to construct in Ohio...

Reuters reports that although details remain unclear, the South Korean company produces RAM and NAND flash memory chips for Apple products.

Some processors used in Apple products are already manufactured in the United States, but because foreign companies are restricted from using TSMC's most advanced processes, these processors can only be used in older models. However, since Apple uses industry-standard versions, DRAM or NAND flash memory chips are not affected by such restrictions.

However, the report also notes that the plan may face opposition from the South Korean government, as South Korea, like Taiwan, may have concerns about exporting chip manufacturing technology, even when it involves older process nodes.

SK hynix said no decision has been made yet. Intel declined to comment on the report but confirmed it will continue to advance the development plan for the Ohio project.
